extracted.intended_audience: industry data analysts, analytics team leads, and reviewer practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Practical framework for running and evaluating peer review processes within analytics teams, including goals, formats, success factors, and adoption metrics. Focuses on making reviews actionable, scalable, and oriented toward error reduction and knowledge sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: "Evaluation of work by one or more people with similar competencies" to maintain quality and catch errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition kept deliberately flexible rather than prescriptive — teams have autonomy in implementation. Purpose: maintain quality and catch errors; adapt process to team needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Error reduction via mistake-catching and approach validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of four core goals for peer review: reviewers check for mistakes and validate analytic approach to improve correctness and reliability of outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous improvement via knowledge-sharing with senior peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review should be used as a learning mechanism: share techniques, reasoning, and feedback to raise analyst skill over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best-practice dissemination
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reviews to spread standards, patterns, and proven approaches between teams to harmonize quality and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability through consistent methodologies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design review processes that can scale (e.g., repeatable formats, shared norms) so more teams can adopt them without excessive overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sparring sessions (review format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sparring sessions — regular meetings where analysts present early work for team feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most popular format; useful for early-stage feedback and collaborative discussion. Good for surfacing approach-level issues and sharing context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code reviews (review format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code reviews — formal pull-request reviews for productionized pipelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when work is productionized; formal, asynchronous, and focuses on code quality, correctness, and maintainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slack channels (review format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Slack channels — informal or structured feedback threads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lightweight channel for quick questions, asynchronous discussion, or centralized feedback threads; can be ad-hoc or governed with structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office hours (review format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office hours — designated weekly slots with assigned reviewers available for consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduled, bounded time for drop-in review and consultation; good for predictable access to senior reviewers and ad-hoc deep-dive help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical success factor: request-specific feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reviewee explicitly asks for the type of feedback that they are looking for."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewees should state the focus (e.g., messaging, analytical methods) to direct reviewer attention and keep feedback actionable. This prevents unfocused or low-utility comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team autonomy in implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the peer-review definition flexible so teams can implement formats that suit them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than a single prescriptive process, allow teams to choose formats and cadence (sparring, code reviews, Slack, office hours) that match their workflows and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption / engagement metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure adoption: percentage of teams engaging with at least one peer-review format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atlassian observation: >90% of analytics teams engaged with at least one peer-review format — use participation as a success metric and to validate scalability despite initial concerns about time and silos.
